one_line: Gond king and Sanskrit poet at Garha-Katanga, united in courtly learning and literary patronage.

appearance.age_look: Sangram Shah appears as a broad-shouldered man in his late 30s to early 40s; Bhanudatta Miśra appears as a slender Brahmin scholar in his mid-30s.
appearance.face: Sangram Shah has an oval face, deep brown complexion, strong jaw, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache, and focused, confident eyes with a calm half-smile; Bhanudatta has a slightly thinner oval face, wheat-brown complexion, fine features, a short moustache and stubble, with bright observant eyes and a thoughtful, gentle expression.
appearance.hair: Sangram Shah’s black hair is medium length, combed back from the forehead and tied low at the nape under a simple dark red turban with a narrow gold border and a small central leaf-shaped ornament; Bhanudatta’s black hair is mostly shaved with a single thick topknot (śikhā) tied at the back of the crown, and he wears no headgear.
appearance.costume: Sangram Shah wears a long knee-length cotton tunic (kurta) in muted cream with a narrow maroon border at cuffs and hem, over a deep forest-green wrapped lower cloth (dhoti-style, pleated in front) tied at the waist, with a rich maroon cotton waist-sash and a diagonally draped light-ochre shawl; over this he has a simple brown leather belt holding a small utility pouch, and he wears plain gold stud earrings, a single medium-width gold bangle on each wrist, and simple brown leather sandals; Bhanudatta wears a plain off-white cotton dhoti wrapped high and neat, paired with a matching long-sleeved angarakha-style upper garment in light beige tied at the side with a thin cord, and a soft, pale-yellow shawl lightly draped over his left shoulder and around his torso in a scholarly manner, with a single thin sacred thread (yajnopavita) implied beneath the angarakha but not exposed, and simple wooden sandals.
appearance.signature: Sangram Shah’s signature prop is a sheathed straight steel sword with a slightly flared Indian hilt and a plain brown scabbard hanging from his belt, while he holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord in his left hand; Bhanudatta’s signature prop is an open palm-leaf manuscript on a low wooden writing board that he cradles, with a stylus tucked into the fold of his shawl.

ref_desc: Sangram Shah is a deep-brown, strong-jawed king with a maroon-bordered cream kurta, forest-green dhoti, dark red turban and sheathed sword plus palm-leaf manuscript, beside wheat-brown scholar Bhanudatta Miśra in off-white dhoti, beige angarakha, pale-yellow shawl and open palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character pair from early 16th-century central India: on the left, Sangram Shah, a broad-shouldered, deep-brown Gond king in his late 30s, with an oval face, strong jaw, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and calm, confident eyes; his black hair is combed back and tied low beneath a simple dark red turban with a narrow gold border and a small leaf-shaped ornament at the front. He wears a knee-length cream cotton kurta with a narrow maroon border at cuffs and hem, over a deep forest-green wrapped dhoti-like lower garment with front pleats, secured by a rich maroon waist-sash; a light-ochre shawl is draped diagonally from his right shoulder across his torso, and a plain brown leather belt with a small pouch cinches his waist. He has plain gold stud earrings, a single medium-width gold bangle on each wrist and simple brown leather sandals. His signature weapon is a sheathed straight steel sword with a slightly flared Indian hilt and plain brown scabbard hanging from his belt, while in his left hand he gently holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord, suggesting both warrior and patron. On the right, draw Bhanudatta Miśra, a slender Brahmin scholar in his mid-30s, wheat-brown complexion, with a slightly narrow oval face, fine features, a short moustache and light stubble, and bright, thoughtful eyes; his head is mostly shaved with a single thick topknot (śikhā) tied at the back of the crown, and no headgear. He wears an off-white cotton dhoti wrapped high and neat, a matching long-sleeved light-beige angarakha-style upper garment tied at the side, and a soft pale-yellow shawl draped from his left shoulder around his torso in a scholarly wrap, with the sacred thread only hinted at under his clothing; he has simple wooden sandals. His signature prop is an open palm-leaf manuscript resting on a low wooden writing board that he cradles in his hands, with a stylus tucked into the fold of his shawl. Use a palette of cream, maroon, forest green, light ochre and pale yellow, keep all clothing modest and era-accurate, and present them standing side by side in a neutral pose like a model sheet, clearly showing face, hairstyle, full garments and their respective sword and manuscript props.
